title: Player count
answer: The CATAN base game is for 3–4 players. The 5–6 player extension has its own rules.

title: Ending the game
answer: You win immediately if you have at least 10 victory points on your own turn. Reaching 10 on someone else’s turn doesn’t end the game; you must still have 10 when your turn comes around.

title: Counting victory points
end: begins the game with 2 victory points.
answer: Count 1 point per settlement, 2 per city, 2 each for Longest Road and Largest Army, and 1 per victory point card. Your two starting settlements give you 2 points.

title: Place the starting pieces
answer: Choose a color and take its 5 settlements, 4 cities, 15 roads, and building-cost card. On the beginner map, place 2 settlements and 2 roads in the pictured positions for your color. With three players, leave red out.

title: Prepare the supply
end: Place the robber in the desert.
answer: Put the five resource piles face up and the shuffled development deck face down. Set both bonus cards and the dice beside the board. Place the robber on the desert.

title: Variable setup: placement order
end: rolls both dice for resource production.
answer: For variable setup, highest roll places a settlement and an adjacent road first. Continue clockwise. The last player places again, then go back in reverse order. Follow the distance rule. Take starting resources from the hexes touching your second settlement. The original starting player rolls first. The second settlement need not connect to the first.

title: A turn in three steps
start: On your turn, you can do
answer: Roll both dice for production, trade if you want, then build or buy development cards. Pass the dice to your left. An eligible development card can also be played during your turn.

Timing of trade versus construction: exchanging resource cards comes before placing a road, settlement or city.
The trade phase comes first; you can swap cards, then put a road on the board during the build phase.

title: Collecting resources
start: There are 5 different types of resources
answer: On a production roll, every player collects from matching, unblocked hexes touching their buildings: 1 resource for each settlement and 2 for each city. It doesn’t have to be your turn.

title: Terrain and resources
answer: Hills give brick, forests give lumber, mountains give ore, fields give grain, and pastures give wool. The desert produces nothing.

title: When the bank runs short
answer: If the supply can’t pay everyone due a particular resource, nobody gets that type. If only one player is affected, they take what remains. Other resource types still pay out.
queries: What if the bank runs out of a resource?

Resource shortage: distributing the remaining supply to one or several players owed cards.

title: Trading with other players
answer: After rolling, the active player may trade resources with other players. Every trade must involve the active player. No gifts, development-card trades, or swaps of a resource for the same type. Bank trades are only on your own turn.

title: Bank trades and harbors
answer: On your turn, give the bank 4 of one resource for 1 of your choice. With a settlement or city on a generic harbor, the rate is 3:1. A specialty harbor gives 2:1 only for the resource shown.

Maritime exchange: identical resource cards at a generic or specialty port.

title: Building a road
answer: Spend 1 brick and 1 lumber. Place the road on an empty edge connected to one of your roads, settlements, or cities.

title: Building a settlement
answer: Spend 1 brick, 1 lumber, 1 wool, and 1 grain. After setup, build on an empty intersection connected to one of your roads. All neighboring intersections must be free of settlements and cities, including your own. It’s worth 1 point.

title: Upgrading to a city
end: Each city is worth 2 victory points.
answer: Spend 3 ore and 2 grain to replace one of your settlements with a city. Return the settlement to your supply. A city is worth 2 points total and collects 2 resources when an adjacent hex produces.

title: Buying development cards
answer: Spend 1 ore, 1 wool, and 1 grain to draw the top development card. Keep it hidden until used. If the deck is empty, you can’t buy one.

title: Playing a development card
answer: Play at most one knight or progress card on your turn, even before rolling. You can’t play one you just bought. The exception is victory point cards: reveal them, including newly bought ones, to declare a win on your turn.

title: Revealing victory point cards
start: You must keep victory point cards hidden.
answer: Keep victory point cards secret until the game ends. On your turn, reveal as many as you need to win, even ones you just bought. You can also show them after someone else wins.

title: Rolling a seven
answer: On a 7, no hex produces. Anyone holding more than 7 resource cards discards half, rounded down. The roller moves the robber to a different hex, then takes one random resource card from an eligible opponent with a building there, if possible.

title: What the robber blocks
end: as long as the robber is in the hex.
answer: The robber starts in the desert. A 7 or a knight moves it. Only the occupied hex is blocked: it gives no resources to any adjacent settlement or city while the robber stays there.

title: Playing a knight
end: If that player has no cards, you get nothing!
answer: Playing a knight moves the robber to a different hex, including the desert. Pick one opponent with a settlement or city there and take a random resource card. If that opponent has none, you get nothing. Leave the knight face up.

title: Largest Army
start: If you are the first player to play 3
answer: The first player with 3 played knights takes Largest Army and 2 points. Another player takes it only by playing more knights than the holder; a tie doesn’t transfer it.

title: Longest Road
start: If you are the first player to build
end: They also acquire the 2 bonus victory points.
answer: The first continuous route of at least 5 road pieces earns Longest Road, worth 2 points. At a fork, count only the longest single route. A challenger must build a longer route; matching the holder’s length isn’t enough.

title: Breaking Longest Road
start: You can break an opponent’s road
answer: A legal settlement can interrupt another player’s road. If the holder still ties for longest at 5 or more, they keep the card. If they fall behind and two others tie for longest, or nobody has 5, set the card aside until a sole qualifying leader emerges.

A rival village cuts your continuous route in two. Recalculate the longest unbroken section to see who keeps the bonus.
Ownership of the Longest Road award after another player builds a settlement in the middle of the route.

title: Monopoly card
answer: Name one resource type. Every other player gives you all cards of that type in their hand; players without it give nothing.

title: Opening tips
start: Brick and lumber are the most important
end: offer trades to the current player!
answer: The rulebook suggests starting near a productive source of brick or lumber and leaving space to expand. A harbor can help if you produce a lot of its resource. These are tips, not placement requirements.

title: Variable board: number tokens
answer: For the lettered layout, begin at a corner and spiral counterclockwise toward the center in alphabetical order, skipping the desert. If you randomize the numbers instead, separate adjacent red numbers. The desert never gets a token.

title: Inside the box
answer: The base box has 19 terrain hexes, 6 frame pieces, 9 harbors, 18 number tokens, 95 resource cards, 25 development cards, 4 building-cost cards, 2 bonus cards, 16 cities, 20 settlements, 60 roads, 2 dice, a robber, and the rulebook.
